name: Paroxysmal Nocturnal Hemoglobinuria

ethnicAssociations: Slightly more common in Southeast Asia

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: ICCS/ISLH Consensus Guidelines for PNH Flow Cytometry

criteria.description: Flow cytometry demonstrating GPI-anchored protein deficiency on granulocytes and/or monocytes (CD55, CD59, FLAER)
PIGA gene somatic mutation in hematopoietic stem cells
History of thrombosis at unusual sites

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Flow cytometry showing a discrete population of GPI-anchor-deficient cells on at least two cell lineages
diagnosticCriteria.notes: PNH clone size varies; subclinical PNH clones are found in aplastic anemia and MDS. Classical PNH, PNH with bone marrow failure, and subclinical PNH are recognized subtypes.

pathognomonic.notes: Classical but not universal; dark urine due to intravascular hemolysis, worse overnight

common.notes: Smooth muscle dystonia from nitric oxide scavenging by free hemoglobin

occasional.notes: Hepatic vein (Budd-Chiari), cerebral, dermal, mesenteric veins

rare.notes: From chronic hemosiderin deposition in kidney

laboratory: Flow cytometry: GPI-anchor-deficient populations (FLAER, CD55, CD59) on granulocytes, monocytes, and red cells
May have concurrent pancytopenia (PNH/aplastic anemia overlap)
imaging: Doppler ultrasound or CT venography for thrombosis evaluation
MRI showing hepatic or renal hemosiderin deposition
CT or MRI for Budd-Chiari syndrome if suspected
genetic: PIGA gene somatic mutation (X-linked; acquired, not inherited)
Clonal expansion of GPI-deficient hematopoietic stem cells
other: Ham test (acidified serum lysis test) - historical, replaced by flow cytometry
Bone marrow biopsy may show hypoplasia in PNH/aplastic anemia overlap

distinguishingFeatures: Aplastic anemia has pancytopenia with hypocellular marrow
Small PNH clones may coexist in aplastic anemia
No significant hemolysis in pure aplastic anemia
No GPI-anchor-deficient population on flow cytometry

redFlags: Thrombosis at unusual sites (hepatic, cerebral, mesenteric veins)
Severe hemolytic crises with renal impairment
Development of severe bone marrow failure
Transformation to myelodysplastic syndrome or acute leukemia
references: Brodsky RA. Paroxysmal nocturnal hemoglobinuria. Blood. 2014;124(18):2804-2811.
Hill A, et al. Under the spotlight: the role of complement in PNH. Blood. 2017;129(12):1570-1577.
Parker CJ. Update on the diagnosis and management of paroxysmal nocturnal hemoglobinuria. Hematology Am Soc Hematol Educ Program. 2016;2016(1):208-216.
Borowitz MJ, et al. Guidelines for the diagnosis and monitoring of paroxysmal nocturnal hemoglobinuria and related disorders by flow cytometry. Cytometry B Clin Cytom. 2010;78(4):211-230.
